title: Heart
summary: The heart is the powerful muscle that pumps blood around the whole body. Explore its four chambers, the valves that keep blood flowing one way, and the double pump that sends blood to the lungs and the rest of the body.

compareCandidate.label: Heart vs. skeletal muscle
compareCandidate.description: The heart is made of special cardiac muscle that beats automatically, never stops, and never gets tired. Skeletal muscles (like your arm) move only when you tell them to and get tired with hard work.

processes: Pumping blood to the lungs to get oxygen
Pumping oxygen-rich blood to the body
Keeping blood flowing one way with valves
plainLanguageExplanation: The heart is a muscular pump about the size of your fist, found in the chest just behind the breastbone. It has four chambers: two smaller ones on top (atria) that receive blood, and two bigger ones below (ventricles) that pump blood out. Valves open and close to keep blood moving in one direction. The heart actually works as a double pump: the right side sends blood to the lungs to pick up oxygen, and the left side pumps the oxygen-rich blood to the whole body. It beats about 60-100 times a minute, day and night, without ever stopping.

whyItMatters: The heart keeps every cell supplied with the oxygen and nutrients blood carries, and it never stops working. Understanding it explains your pulse, how exercise strengthens your heart, and why heart health matters.
didYouKnow: Your heart beats about 100,000 times a day - enough to pump blood through around 96,000 kilometers of blood vessels.
